featured_reviews.name: raunaque sidana
featured_reviews.review_text:
Orlem is a neighbourhood in Malad, a suburb of Mumbai, India. The name "Orlem" is often colloquially used for the Our Lady of Lourdes parish in Malad, which includes Orlem and its neighboring areas. The original name of Orlem in the official language of the state (Marathi) is Valnai. The Indian postal zip code 400064 serves the Orlem neighborhood.
Orlem was one of the many East India villages that existed in Malad. In the 19th century, Orlem was a hamlet of 12 families. The families were the D'limas, D'souzas, etc. Its inhabitants were primarily engaged in agriculture and fishing.
Orlem originally primarily consisted of a population of Roman Catholics. The main ethnic group within the Catholic community were East Indians followed by Goans, Mangloreans and other regional communities. Joseph Maria Braz de Souza, of the Principal family of Valnai, built a private chapel at his own expense in 1880 dedicated to Our Lady of Lourdes at Orlem. He was a former chaplain of military forces at Satara from 1861 to 1886.
In 1882, Bishop Leo Meurin declared officially that this chapel, under the chaplainship of Fr. D'Souza was part of the Apostolate of Bombay and affiliated to the church of Our Lady of Assumption, Kandivali. In 1908, Fr. D'Souza was elevated to the dignity of CAMARIERE SEGREDO EXTRA URBEM to Pius X. He died in December 1912 and was buried in the sanctuary of the chapel that he built. As per the wishes of Msgr. J.M.B. D'Souza, in his will, that a priest from his family should be his successor, Fr. Justin D'Souza was lent by the Bishop of Daman to the Archdiocese of Bombay and appointed Chaplain at Orlem. He carried on the good work of Msgr. D'Souza and his brother Fr. Elias who bequeathed all his properties to the church. Fr. Justin built the first school, the St Anne's High School, in 1915. Through his efforts, Orlem was constituted a separate parish, in a decree dated 2 July 1916.
Fr. Justin extended the church and was assisted in this effort by Mrs. Mary Magdalene D'Souza who financed the elevation for the choir. Fr. Justin also donated all his lands to the Archdiocese and, the Cardinal Gracias Colony later developed on the land that Fr. Justin had donated for the welfare of Orlem. The parish priests that helped to raise Orlem to its present stature include Fr. Herman Mendes, Fr. Celestine Fonseca, Fr. Walter D’Souza, Msgr. Staney Pereira, Fr. Peter C. Gomes and Fr. Frank Noronha, who ventured to start the construction of the new school building in 1959. In the year 1976, Fr. Octavian Dias worked hard to make possible a new extension to the school, a Parochial House and the new Church.
Since the Solemn Inauguration of the new Church on Sunday 6 June 1976, by the then Rt. Rev. Dr, Simon Pimenta, Auxiliary Bishop of Bombay, there has been a huge rise in the Catholic population (highest in the whole world in terms of per parish.
Although Orlem now boasts of being a highly developed commercial as well as residential area, it still maintains its original ambiance. It has come a long way from being a simple village to one of the most attractive places in Bombay (Mumbai). The borders of Orlem are not clearly defined nor is it considered to be a matter of debate or concern. Orlem is sometimes considered to be the umbrella of the other smaller villages of Kharodi, Kanchpada, Rathodi etc. Today Kharodi and Rathodi do not belong to the Orlem parish.
As there is no known origin of the name Orlem, besides "Our Lady Malad", a popular nursery rhyme is often attributed to its origin.
(Extract from Google)

featured_reviews.name: Taslim Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's one of the historical Church.
With a very old school named St.Anthony High school.
Famous for its discipline and education.
Fees is also reasonable as it's an aided school.
Good place for sports which nowadays hardly some schools have.
Lot of greenery is around.
Very soothing place for inner peace.

featured_reviews.name: Nathan Monteiro
featured_reviews.review_text: A beautiful church⛪️ that has been standing for more than 200 years. This church is famous for its architecture and relics of saints who have died in the past are present here. Also the faith of the people is required that God has made in us is also the reason why this church and the churches around the world are standing still because of the christian God - Jesus Christ who died for the sins of the world and rose again from the dead is alive and loves the world. For anyone who is interested should go see this church and they will love it😍.

featured_reviews.name: Shahab Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Don't know about the school. went there for parties/wedding many times. Ground is elegant. Good space for parking as well. Probably one of the best hall for marriages and parties in malwani, Marve, aksa and nearby areas.

featured_reviews.name: Royal Noronha
featured_reviews.review_text: St. Anthony's church is famous for it's St.Anthony's feast which they celebrate once a year....People come here from other parishes.....sweet buns are distributed after the mass.... The population in this parish is increasing as people are moving to this place.....The church is also being re renovated, so I guess they will extant the area.

featured_reviews.name: Jasmine Johnson
featured_reviews.review_text: When I found there is a Marthoma Church so close to my house after 3 yrs of living near it I was so happy & I went there few months back to enquire about the church timings but the way I was treated by the watchman I would suggest never ever go there. it's a place of worship not anyone's private property.. everyone has the right to visit the Church & what if it's a Malayalee Church aren't people from another belief and community accepted here? Is this how u train ur gaurds to treat another people who show interest to come and pray?? While u preach for heaven ?double standard huh? I was stopping myself from posting this here but every Sunday I miss the service and this Marthoma Church will be responsible for it..
